items.q: How do I book a charter?
items.a: Book directly through the website, or call or text Capt. Chad at (386) 853-4814. Let him know what you're after (inshore, nearshore, shark fishing or a tour) and he'll match the trip type and timing to the best tide for that day.

items.q: What's included in the trip price?
items.a: Every charter includes your Florida fishing license, all rods, tackle and bait, plus a cooler, ice and bottled water on board. Fish cleaning is included for in season species once you're back at the dock. Pricing varies by charter type and trip length, so call or book online for current rates.

items.q: Do you require a deposit to book?
items.a: Most trips require a deposit to hold your date. Exact amounts vary by charter type and length. Book online or call Capt. Chad to confirm the deposit for your trip, especially during busier seasons when dates fill up fast.

items.q: What payment methods do you accept?
items.a: Call Capt. Chad at (386) 853-4814 or check the online booking page to confirm which payment methods are accepted before your trip.

items.q: What's your cancellation policy?
items.a: If you need to cancel or reschedule, give Capt. Chad as much notice as possible so he can rebook the slot. Cancellations due to weather are always fully refunded or rescheduled at no cost.

items.q: Do you offer gift certificates?
items.a: Yes. Gift certificates are available for any Reel Deal Fishin' charter or tour and are easy to purchase directly through Capt. Chad. They make a great gift for experienced anglers and first timers alike.

items.q: Do I need a fishing license to book a charter?
items.a: No. Every Reel Deal Fishin' charter includes your Florida fishing license, so there's nothing to buy or arrange beforehand. Just show up ready to fish.

items.q: What should I bring with me?
items.a: Bring polarized sunglasses, sunscreen and a camera. The gear itself is covered. Pack snacks and drinks for the ride, and a light jacket if you're heading out on a cool morning or a night trip.

items.q: Can I bring my own rod?
items.a: Yes. If you've got a favorite rod and reel, bring it along and Capt. Chad will work with your setup. If not, every charter already includes rods, tackle and bait.

items.q: Do you clean and bag the fish we catch?
items.a: Yes. Fish cleaning is included at the dock for all in season inshore species once your trip wraps up.

items.q: Are your trips good for kids and beginners?
items.a: Absolutely. Inshore trips run in calm, protected water that makes it easy to learn, and Capt. Chad gives hands on coaching on casting and handling fish. It's built for beginners and kids to actually catch something, not just watch.

items.q: What happens if the weather is bad?
items.a: If conditions aren't safe to run, Capt. Chad will reschedule your trip or refund you. He watches the marine forecast closely and would rather move a date than put anyone on the water in bad weather.

items.q: Do people get seasick on your trips?
items.a: Rarely. Most Reel Deal Fishin' charters run in calm, protected inshore water with minimal swell, and even the nearshore trips stay close to the beach. If you're prone to motion sickness, an inshore trip is the safest bet.

items.q: Are life jackets provided?
items.a: Yes. Every charter carries all required U.S. Coast Guard safety gear, including life jackets sized for adults and children. Just let Capt. Chad know if kids will be on board.

items.q: How many people can you take on a trip?
items.a: Up to 6 guests per trip, and every trip is private, your group only. Prices include a set number of guests with a small charge for each extra guest. See trip prices.

items.q: Do you run private or shared charters?
items.a: All Reel Deal Fishin' charters are private. It's just you, your group and the captain, never combined with another party.

items.q: Can we request a specific type of fishing?
items.a: Sure. Whether you're after redfish on the flats, a relaxed family outing or something with more pull like shark or nearshore fishing, Capt. Chad builds the day around what you want.

items.q: Can you handle special occasions?
items.a: Yes. Reel Deal Fishin' has hosted birthdays, family reunions and couples outings. Let Capt. Chad know what you're celebrating when you book, and he'll help plan a trip that fits.

items.q: Can we book a sightseeing only trip?
items.a: Yes. We run dolphin and manatee tours and, when the glow is on, nighttime bioluminescence tours for guests who want to be on the water without fishing.

items.q: What fish are biting in Daytona and New Smyrna Beach right now?
items.a: It changes with the tides and the season, but we regularly put anglers on redfish, trout, snook, flounder, sheepshead and drum, plus sharks and other nearshore species when they're running. Check our fishing reports for dated updates.

items.q: What's the best time of year to fish in Daytona and New Smyrna Beach?
items.a: Spring and fall bring the strongest action, but fishing runs year round. Spring means redfish and cobia, summer turns on snook and tarpon, fall is prime for flounder and drum, and winter brings sheepshead along the docks and bridges.

items.q: Do you keep fish on your trips?
items.a: Yes, for in season species like redfish, trout, flounder and sheepshead, following Florida's size and bag limits. Sharks are catch and release only on every trip.

items.q: What species can we target on an inshore charter?
items.a: Redfish, snook, trout, flounder, sheepshead and drum in the calm, protected backwaters around New Smyrna Beach. Capt. Chad adjusts the plan to the season and the day's bite.

items.q: What do you catch nearshore?
items.a: Sharks, kingfish, tarpon, jacks and cobia when they're running, just a few miles off the beach.

items.q: How far do you run on nearshore trips?
items.a: Most nearshore trips run just a few miles off the beach, close enough that you're never far from the coast.

items.q: When is the best time for shark fishing?
items.a: Shark trips run May 1 through November 1, and summer is peak. Sharks also turn up on nearshore trips outside that window.

items.q: Where do your trips leave from?
items.a: Charters launch from New Smyrna Beach, FL, a short drive from Daytona Beach and minutes from the Indian River Lagoon, Mosquito Lagoon and the nearshore Atlantic.

items.q: How early should we arrive before the trip?
items.a: Plan to arrive 10 to 15 minutes before your departure time. That gives Capt. Chad time to run through safety basics and get everyone settled.
